newsitem.title: CANADA: Avenor lowers bid for Repap.
newsitem.headline: Avenor lowers bid for Repap.

text.p: Avenor Inc said on Monday that it lowered its bid for Repap Enterprises Inc to one newly issued share of Avenor for every eight common shares of Repap from the 1-for-4.25 shares originally offered.

Avenor also said that Repap British Columbia Inc. (Repap B.C.) and its C$480 million of debt (C$620 million of total liabilities) will be excluded from the revised all-stock bid for Repap. With the removal of Repap B.C., Avenor will not proceed with the originally planned C$75 million private placements of additional common shares and C$140 million issue of convertible subordinated debentures, it said.

As a result, the dilution in Avenor shares will be further reduced under the revised offer, Avenor said. The existing C$50 million guarantee in favor of Repap B.C. banks as well as about C$22 million of other financial obligations will be honored, the company said.

Avenor said its board of directors and the Repap board agreed on the amended terms of the merger agreement. A special meeting of Avenor shareholders originally scheduled for March 12 will be postponed to March 26.
Avenor said the amended agreement benefits all shareholders of the new Avenor.

"These changes will allow the Company to focus more rapidly on the coated paper business with its higher profit margins, less volatile pricing and better growth prospects," said Avenor President and Chief Executive Officer Paul Gagne.
"Furthermore, the removal of Repap B.C. frm the transaction contributes to reduce both the debt level and the share dilution caused by the transaction," he said.

Avenor said remains committed to its debt reduction plan and will divest its British Columbia operations and the Repap Manitoba kraft paper mill for estimated combined gross proceeds of C$500 million within 18 months of the merger.
Avenor said it will also achieve annual operating synergies resulting from the acquisition that are now estimated at over C$112 million, once fully implemented by the end of 1998.

Repap Chairman and Chief Executive Officer George Petty said: "Recognizing the additional value created through reduced risk, leverage and dilution in the merged company under the revised terms, Repap's Board of Directors and I support the terms of the new transaction. New Avenor will have the critical mass to become a world-class, flexible producer of high value paper grades through this merger."

Avenor said a supplement to the Joint Management Proxy Circular will be mailed to Avenor and Repap shareholders in the next few days and will be available on the Internet at http://www.avenor.com after 1300 EST/1800 GMT Monday.
Avenor said senior management will hold a conference call Monday with industry analysts at 1130 EST/1630 GMT to outline the details of the new transaction. ((Reuters Montreal bureau 514-985-2434))
